MY LEAF STUDIO

Look Closely at My Leaf

Become a leaf detective: the tip, the edge, the veins and the stem.

Look, then try.

Choose one leaf and give it your full attention. Look at the tip first: is it pointed like a pencil or rounded like a pebble? Follow the edge with your finger. Hold the leaf up to the light and find the veins: a strong middle line with smaller lines branching away, like a tree in miniature. A magnifying glass helps, but curious eyes are enough. Draw the lines you actually see, not the leaf you imagine. Real leaves are crooked and surprising, and that is what makes them interesting.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps with scissors when cutting out rubbings. Collect fallen leaves from the ground, or pick with permission, and brush off dirt and insects. Wash hands after handling leaves. Nothing you find outside goes in your mouth.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Meet my leaf

Draw your leaf big, filling the whole box. Start with the outline, then add the stem.

ACTIVITY 2

Follow the veins

Hold the leaf up to the light. Trace the middle vein, then the branches coming off it.

ACTIVITY 3

The surprise

Every leaf hides something: a hole, a freckle, a wiggly edge. Draw the surprise you found.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Leaves have parts with jobs: the stem carries water, veins spread it through the leaf, and the surface catches light. Drawing from real observation trains attention better than copying a picture.
